comment: Free stand-ins for Garmin's system fonts and device-resident scalable faces (docs/research/10-system-fonts.md, docs/research/40-vector-face-stand-ins.md). Resolution order: names (exact: every scalable face name and file stem the SDK device reference publishes) -> patterns (ordered, first match wins) -> faces (last resort, keyed by the scraped device-reference 'face' column). Every source is pinned (URL, SHA-256, size) and carries its licence; 'match' says how close the file is to Garmin's own: exact (the same cut), family (the same free family, another weight, version or Garmin's tweaked build) or substitute (a different typeface for a proprietary face). 'unmapped' lists names deliberately left unresolved (none today).

roboto-condensed-bold.note: The device's own RobotoCondensed-Bold is this design: the SDK Manager's copy is Google's 2014 v2.000980 build, this the v2.138 release, with the same advances on 95% of the shared glyphs and on every ASCII letter and digit. Also the substitute behind Bionic Cond, Chronos, Steelfish, Phelant and Digi (their own keys).

roboto-condensed-regular.note: The device's own RobotoCondensed-Regular is this design (Google's v2.000980 there, v2.138 here; the same advances on every ASCII letter and digit).

roboto-condensed-medium.note: Same family/release as roboto-condensed-bold; used for the 'M'-suffixed CDPG_ROBOTO bitmap tokens.

roboto-light.note: Face 'Roboto Light'; also used for the VENU_BOLD_NUMBER_FONT_6/7 scrape anomaly (filename says BOLD, scraped face column says Roboto Light -- trusted the face column).

roboto-bold.note: No device ships a file literally named Roboto-Bold; this is the same Apache-2.0 Roboto family's Bold static instance, used for 'Garmin Robo Units' (Garmin_Roboto_Bold and 006B416900_ROBOTO_BOLD_* bitmaps) and other bare *_ROBOTO_BOLD_* tokens.

roboto-black.note: Byte-identical to the device's own Roboto-Black TTF (fr955 FONT_NUMBER_HOT/THAI_HOT; scalable RobotoBlack on one device).

roboto-italic.note: Face scraped as 'Roboto Wide', file Roboto-Italic on every device that has it: Garmin's build of Roboto Italic v2.137 with wider advances (digits 0.562 em, Roboto Italic's 0.545). This is Roboto Italic v2.138.

bebas-neue-regular.note: Google Fonts ships Bebas Neue as a single 'Regular' style that is itself the heavy display weight Garmin's docs call 'Bebas Neue Bold' / '...DJV Glyph ttf' / '...ttf'.

rajdhani-medium.note: Garmin's Bionic Medium (BionicMedium; file Bionic_Medium, whose face column the reference gives as 'Rajdhani') is Rajdhani Medium with tabular digits (0.500 em), every other shared glyph Rajdhani's outline (docs/research/40-vector-face-stand-ins.md).

yantramanav-regular.note: The one scraped filename 'Yantramanav-Regular' under face 'Yantramanav'.

oswald-variable.note: Google Fonts ships Oswald only as a wght 200-700 variable font; Garmin's nominal 'Oswald Light' weight is approximated by whichever instance a plain (non-variation-aware) loader resolves, not pinned to the light end of the axis. hhea ascent/descent do not vary across the wght axis in this build (checked), so the *metric* model is unaffected -- only the rendered stroke weight is approximate.

noto-sans-variable.note: Google Fonts ships Noto Sans only as a wght/wdth variable font; same default-instance caveat as oswald-variable. Used for face 'Noto Sans' (Latin-script bold numerals on aviation devices, not the CJK 'Noto Sans SC' family, which stays unmapped).

dejavu-sans-bold.note: Face 'Garmin': the generic label Garmin's own docs use for the DejaVu-derived bitmap numeral fonts on Edge/GPSMAP cycling and hiking computers (DEJAVU_FITNESS_*, GPSMAP66_DEJAVU_REC_*, 006B345900_FNT_0000_PRO_*, DejaVuGarmin_Rec_with_bionic_numbers). The scraped file name literally contains 'DEJAVU', so the real file is some DejaVu derivative; DejaVu Sans Bold is the closest still-free relative for these non-condensed number faces.

dejavu-sans-condensed-bold.note: Face 'DejaVu Sans Medium Condensed B' (006B416900_DEJA_VU_SANS_*, DEJAVU_SANS_*, GPSMAP66_DEJAVU_SANS_*, DejaVuSans_Cd_SemiBold_WGL4). DejaVu ships an official Condensed-Bold cut of the same family; 'Medium' in Garmin's label is read as normal (non-light) weight, not DejaVu's separate 'Medium' style (which does not exist).

bionic-cond-substitute.note: Proprietary 'Bionic Cond' number face. Substitute picked because the very same devices (fenix8solar47mm, marq2, ...) use RobotoCondensed-Bold for their own FONT_XTINY..LARGE body text; condensed bold weight/width is the closest free match for a condensed numeral face.

bionic-substitute.note: Bionic's bitmap number fonts (*_BIONIC_BOLD_NUMBER_*, face 'Bionic') and the face column 'Bionic': Bionic is Garmin's tabular-digit build of Rajdhani (rajdhani-bold's note), so Rajdhani Bold. The condensed bitmaps (BIONIC_COND) have their own key.

chronos-substitute.note: Proprietary 'Chronos' number face (fenix5 era). Substitute picked because fenix5's own FONT_XTINY..LARGE body text is Roboto Condensed (Bold/Regular).

steelfish-substitute.note: Proprietary 'Steelfish' number face (d2bravo, fenix3). Substitute picked because the same devices' own body text is Roboto Condensed.

phelant-substitute.note: Proprietary 'Phelant' number face (epix, vivoactive). Substitute picked because the same devices' own body text is Roboto Condensed.

digi-substitute.note: Proprietary 7-segment-style 'Digi' face (fr920xt). Weakest substitute in this registry: fr920xt uses Digi for its *entire* font table, so there is no free same-device sibling family to borrow, unlike Bionic/Chronos/Steelfish/Phelant. A dedicated 7-segment OFL face (e.g. DSEG7) would fit better and is a documented follow-up, skipped here to keep the download scope sane for a single legacy device.

digi-narrow-substitute.note: Proprietary 'Digi Narrow' face (fr920xt FONT_NUMBER_MILD only). Same weak-substitute caveat as digi-substitute.

roboto-condensed-italic.note: Scalable face RobotoCondensedRegularItalic (file RobotoCondensed-RegularItalic, 6 devices). Garmin's file is Google's v2.137 Roboto Condensed Italic with tabular digits widened to 0.484 em; this is the v2.138 italic of the same release as roboto-condensed-bold (bounding boxes agree on 99% of shared glyphs; docs/research/40-vector-face-stand-ins.md).

rajdhani-bold.note: Garmin's Bionic Bold (BionicBold; files Bionic_Bold, Bionic_Bold_Number_Only, 43 devices) is Rajdhani Bold renamed, with its digits and '+' redrawn to one tabular width (0.516 em; Rajdhani's are proportional, '1' 0.334 em): every other shared glyph has Rajdhani's outline, the version string, vendor ITFO and OFL notice are Rajdhani's (docs/research/40-vector-face-stand-ins.md).

rajdhani-semibold.note: Garmin's Bionic SemiBold (BionicSemiBold/BionicSemibold; file Bionic_semibold, the fenix 8 FONT_NUMBER_* face) is Rajdhani SemiBold with tabular digits (0.516 em), every other shared glyph Rajdhani's outline (docs/research/40-vector-face-stand-ins.md).

noto-sans-sc-medium.note: Noto Sans SC Medium v1.004 (Adobe's CFF OpenType, installed under a .ttf name), the release every Garmin NotoSansSC-Medium file was converted from: advances and bounding boxes agree on every shared glyph; Garmin's -2/-3/-Outdoor builds drop about 600 glyphs, none redrawn. 8.4 MB, the registry's largest file (docs/research/40-vector-face-stand-ins.md).

noto-sans-hebrew-regular.note: Byte-identical to Garmin's NotoSansHebrew-Regular (v1.04). Hebrew only: no Latin letters or digits.

noto-sans-hebrew-bold.note: Byte-identical to Garmin's NotoSansHebrew-Bold (v1.04). Hebrew only: no Latin letters or digits.

kosugi-regular.note: Garmin's face family 'MotoyaLCedar' is Google's Kosugi (Motoya L Cedar). Kosugi-Regular and -3 have this file's advances and bounding boxes on every shared glyph; -2 and -Outdoor (34 of the 57 devices) also redraw the 58 half-width katakana (docs/research/40-vector-face-stand-ins.md).

nanumgothic-regular.note: Same NanumGothic v3.020 outlines and advances; Garmin's build moves every glyph about 0.044 em down, changes hhea, and adds about 5,600 codepoints this file lacks (docs/research/40-vector-face-stand-ins.md).

nanumgothic-bold.note: Same NanumGothic Bold v3.020 outlines and advances; Garmin's build moves every glyph 0.051 em down, changes hhea, and adds about 5,600 codepoints this file lacks.

nanumgothic-extrabold.note: Same NanumGothic ExtraBold v3.020 outlines and advances; Garmin's build moves every glyph down, changes hhea, and adds about 5,600 codepoints this file lacks.

pridi-regular.note: Pridi Regular v1.001: the same outlines and advances as Garmin's Pridi-Regular on every shared glyph (not byte-identical).

pridi-regular-garmin.note: Garmin's Pridi-Regular_Garmin redraws 20 Thai glyphs of Pridi Regular v1.001 (and the tone marks); this is the unmodified Pridi Regular.

pridi-semibold-garmin.note: Garmin's Pridi-SemiBold_Garmin redraws 7 Thai glyphs of Pridi SemiBold v1.001; this is the unmodified Pridi SemiBold.

amiri-regular.note: Sakkal Majalla (Microsoft's, Sakkal Design) is proprietary. Amiri, a Naskh face, is closest by look of the five free Arabic faces compared: its letterforms, Arabic-Indic digits and serif Latin digits are nearest Sakkal's; it draws about 25% larger on the same em (docs/research/40-vector-face-stand-ins.md).

amiri-bold.note: Sakkal Majalla Bold is proprietary; Amiri Bold, as amiri-regular (docs/research/40-vector-face-stand-ins.md).

arimo-regular.note: Swis721Hebrew BT (Bitstream's Helvetica-style Swiss 721 with Hebrew) is proprietary. Arimo is Helvetica-proportioned Latin plus Hebrew in one file (Noto Sans Hebrew lacks Latin and digits); on the sample its width at the same em is within 3% (docs/research/40-vector-face-stand-ins.md).

arimo-bold.note: Swis721Hebrew BT Bold is proprietary; Arimo Bold, as arimo-regular (docs/research/40-vector-face-stand-ins.md).

exo-semibold.note: Exo SemiBold, the 2016 refresh of Exo 1.0 that Google Fonts serves. Garmin's Exo-SemiBold (3 aviation devices) is not on this machine to compare, and Exo exists in two spacings, hence family.

tomorrow-bold.note: Tomorrow Bold v2.002, the only free release of the face. Garmin's Tomorrow-Bold (marq2aviator) is not on this machine to compare (UNVERIFIED by bytes).

fenix5/fenix5x FNT_FENIX5_ROBOTOCONDENSEDBOLD_{26,29,34,37}PX -- no underscore between ROBOTO and CONDENSED, unlike the ROBOTO_CONDENSED family above; scraped face is 'Roboto Condensed', filename says BOLD explicitly (.cache/device-reference/devices/fenix5.json FONT_TINY..LARGE).
fenix5/fenix5x FNT_FENIX5_ROBOTOCONDENSEDREGULAR_26PX (FONT_XTINY/FONT_SYSTEM_XTINY); filename says REGULAR explicitly, so the regular key is used rather than the bold-assumed default.

vivoactive4/vivoactive4s FNT_VIVOACTIVE4[S]_ROBOTO_{XTINY,TINY,TINY_PLUS,SMALL}_BOLD -- scraped face for FONT_XTINY..SMALL is 'Roboto Condensed' (.cache/device-reference/devices/vivoactive4.json), filename drops CONDENSED but says BOLD explicitly. MEDIUM/MEDIUM_PLUS siblings already resolve via the ROBOTO_MEDIUM pattern above and are left alone.

venu FNT_VENU_ROBOTO_{LARGE,LARGE_PLUS}_BOLD (FONT_MEDIUM/FONT_LARGE) -- scraped face is 'Roboto Condensed' (.cache/device-reference/devices/venu.json), the same naming as the vivoactive4 pattern above: CONDENSED dropped, BOLD stated. Its TINY/SMALL siblings already match that pattern; FNT_VENU_ROBOTO_MEDIUM_BOLD resolves via ROBOTO_MEDIUM above, left alone like vivoactive4's.

vivoactive4/vivoactive4s FNT_VIVOACTIVE4[S]_REGULAR_NUMBER_FONT_{1,2} (FONT_NUMBER_MILD/_MEDIUM) -- scraped face is 'Roboto Condensed' (.cache/device-reference/devices/vivoactive4.json) and the filename states REGULAR explicitly, unlike the unweighted NUMBER_FONT_* ladder above where bold is only assumed for lack of a stated weight.
